public_rationale: The larger-task failure is accurately described: both VLA configurations achieved zero full-task success on unseen four-block Hanoi. But working fine overstates smaller full-puzzle performance: success was only 34% for the end-to-end configuration and zero for the planner-guided configuration. Individual moves were easier, but they are not complete small Hanoi puzzles. The study supports a limited analogy, not an identical mechanism across model classes.
limitations: The mixed outcome depends on the ordinary reliability reading of working fine.
Marcus supplies the 34% figure in the surrounding text, which makes the qualification visible to readers.
Results concern simulated manipulation and two configurations of one VLA family.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: VLA models suffer the same generalization failures on Tower of Hanoi as LLMs, working on small instances but breaking down as size grows.

statement.excerpt: First it (conceptually) replicates and extends the Apple reasoning paper, by showing that a newer variant on LLMs, called VLAs –Vision-Language-Action models, which are increasingly popular in robotics — also suffer from the same generalization problems on the Tower Hanoi, similarly working fine on small versions of the problem but breaking down as more rings get added.
statement.document_title: Even more good news for the future of neurosymbolic AI

from_speaker: breaking down as more rings get added
our_interpretation: This is a claim about the VLA configurations evaluated in the named Tufts study, not every VLA architecture.
Same problems means a similar size-related failure pattern, not proof of an identical underlying mechanism.
Working fine on small versions ordinarily means reasonably reliable completion of smaller full Hanoi tasks, rather than occasional success or isolated block moves.
The target is the February 2026 study reporting period identified in the post.
criteria.support_condition: The study reports substantial success on smaller complete Hanoi tasks followed by failure on larger, unseen tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The larger tasks remain reliably solvable, or the models already fail frequently on the smaller complete tasks. The latter contradicts the working-fine component without disproving larger-task failure.
